name: EZIOxx
description: The EZIOxx I/O controllers from Compacta International, sold as SimpleHomeNet and later Smartenit products: EZIO8SA, EZIO2X4 5010D, EZIO4O 5010J, EZIO6I and EZIO8T. The line runs from inputs-only to outputs-only models, and a model supports only the commands its inputs and outputs need. Inputs send group commands, outputs are relays or other switches, and settings are read and written with the device's own commands and Peek and Poke rather than operating flags.

valueTables.name: responderAction
valueTables.description: What a responder record's middle data byte has the device do when its controller's group On arrives.

values.label: Turn on one output, 0x00 through 0x07 in the lower byte for outputs 1 to 8
Trigger one input as if it went from off to on, 0x00 through 0x06 in the lower byte for inputs 1 to 7
Set the outputs to the pattern in the lower byte, 1 on and 0 off
Turn on the outputs set in the lower byte, leaving the rest

standardCommands.name: readOutputTimers
standardCommands.description: EZIO Control, Get Output Timers: reads the output timers. They arrive in an extended message with cmd1 0x4F and cmd2 0x04, D1 through D8 the timers of outputs 1 through 8.

verification.note: The EZIOxx Advanced Details list Get Output Timers both as this EZIO Control sub-command and as an extended message with cmd1 0x4F and cmd2 0x04 carrying D1 through D8; that the message answers the sub-command is read from their names.

standardCommands.description: EZIO Control, Enable status change message: the device broadcasts when its output port changes.

standardCommands.description: EZIO Control, Disable status change message: the device stops broadcasting output port changes.

standardCommands.name: diagnosticsOn
standardCommands.description: EZIO Control, Diagnostics ON: cycles the outputs on for 1 second each.

standardCommands.name: diagnosticsOff
standardCommands.description: EZIO Control, Diagnostics OFF: takes the device out of diagnostics.

standardCommands.name: setAddressMsb
standardCommands.description: Set Address MSB: sets the high byte of the address Peek and Poke use. It must be 0x00 for the addresses the notes list.

standardCommands.name: poke
standardCommands.description: Poke: writes cmd2 to the parameter RAM at the address Peek last set. A location marked rw keeps the value once Update EEPROM saves it.

standardCommands.name: peek
standardCommands.description: Peek: sets the address to cmd2, and reads the byte there. The notes list the addresses.

extendedCommands.name: setOutputTimers
extendedCommands.description: Set Output Timers: sets the timers of outputs 1 through 8. A timer greater than 0 turns its output off when it runs out, while the Configuration Port's outputTimersEnabled bit is set; the outputTimersInSeconds bit picks seconds or minutes.

notes: The EZIOxx Advanced Details (Rev 2.3, 2016) apply to firmware 2.0 and above. They give EZIO the category 0x07 and subcategory 0x02; Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives each model its own subcategory.

Each input sends a group command when it changes, to the group stored for it at addresses 0x40 through 0x47 (inputs 1 to 8), which needn't match the input's number; several inputs can share a group. An input that isn't linked sends a broadcast instead, when broadcasts are enabled. The commands sent on the off-to-on and on-to-off transitions default to Insteon On and Off and can be changed, at addresses 0x20 through 0x3F.

An input can have a timer, 1 second to 255 minutes, that starts when the input turns on and sends the on-to-off command when it runs out; the device can ignore the input turning off while the timer runs. An input can also switch its corresponding output directly (the inputs-to-outputs crosslink at address 0x1A).

Inputs are digital, analog or 1-Wire (one DS18B20 temperature sensor). An analog or 1-Wire input reads as on while its value is past its alarm point; its off-to-on and on-to-off alarm points are separate counts from 0 to 1023, which gives it hysteresis. Analog inputs read 0 to 5 V or 0 to 3.3 V depending on the model.

Besides the Configuration Port, the Utility Suite sets a Configuration Register: Enable Analog Inputs, Continuous A/D Conversion (once a second rather than when read), Debounce the Inputs, Enable 1-W Sensor, Set Timers in Seconds and Broadcast on Status Change.

As a responder, the device reads the middle and lower data bytes of its link record when a group On arrives: it turns on one output, sets or turns on a pattern of outputs (the snapshot taken when the link was made), or triggers one of its inputs as if it had turned on, which then sends that input's group command if the input is linked. With output timers enabled, an output turns off when its timer runs out, for pulses as short as 1 second.

Status Changed broadcast (cmd1 0x27): when broadcasts are enabled, the device sends the output or input port's byte in cmd2 when it changes, with 00 in the To Address's low byte for the output port and 01 for the input port.

The device answers an ID Request with an acknowledgment and a SET Button Pressed broadcast, without entering linking mode. ALL-Link Activate (cmd1 0x11, an ALL-Link command) recalls groups 0x00 through 0x0F.

Peek and Poke addresses, with Set Address MSB 0x00: 0x00 to 0x07 output timers (rw); 0x08 X10 house code (rw); 0x09 Configuration Port (rw); 0x0A to 0x11 sensor 1 to 4 alarms, 2 bytes each (rw); 0x12 to 0x19 analog inputs 1 and 2 alarms, 4 bytes each (rw); 0x1A inputs-to-outputs crosslink bitmap (rw); 0x1B to 0x1F reserved; 0x20 to 0x3F the group command on/off sequence for inputs 1 to 8 (rw); 0x40 to 0x47 group numbers for inputs 1 to 8 (rw); 0x48 firmware version (r); 0x49 EEPROM loaded flag (r); 0x4A output port status (r); 0x4B input port status (r); 0x4C analog data, 2 bytes for each of 2 inputs (r); 0x50 1-Wire raw data (r); 0x58 to 0x5F input timers (rw). A Poke to an rw location lasts once Update EEPROM saves it.

X10: units 1 to 8 turn outputs 1 to 8 on and off, and unit 16 On and Off enable and disable the output timers. To enable X10, pick a house code (A to P) on an X10 controller, hold the SET button at least 4 seconds and release it so the LED blinks, then send 3 On commands (any unit) until the LED stops blinking; 3 Off commands disable it. The EZIO2X4 5010D and EZIO4O 5010J guides give one On or Off command instead of 3.
